warnings.message: Same full target sentence is reused across multiple scored activities.

manualReview.scope: Model/editor semantic and pedagogy review of production Lesson 0026 authored from curriculum spec en-fa-A1-LESSON-SPEC-0026; not an independent human or learner test.

englishNaturalness.evidence: At a reception desk, What time? / At six. followed by Room one? / No. We are in room two. is a plausible compact schedule-confirmation exchange when the program is already the shared topic.

persianMeaningQuality.evidence: Persian consistently distinguishes the group meaning of we from singular I and expresses time and room location without adding unsupported meaning.

pedagogicalClarity.evidence: We are is the only new grammar target; all lexical items are explicit reviews, and the lesson clearly contrasts group location with the earlier room-choice function.

distractorQuality.evidence: Distractors contrast singular versus group reference, time versus room interpretation, and choosing a room versus stating group location.

dialoguePlausibility.evidence: Nina and Iris continue the established community-center arc from Lesson 20; confirming another program's time and group location gives We are a concrete referent: Nina plus her group.

difficultyFit.evidence: The lesson adds one short A1.1 grammar pattern while reusing known time and room language, keeping new cognitive load low.

repetitionUsefulness.evidence: At six returns after several intervening lessons; room one/two are deliberately reused again but move from recent first-person location negation into affirmative group location, changing both speaker perspective and communicative function.

transferQuality.evidence: The learner moves from selecting or correcting Room one/two to stating where the group is and must change room two to room one in final hidden-answer retrieval.

overallCoherence.evidence: Scenario, schedule review, group-location grammar, exact-audio reconstruction and changed-filler retrieval all serve one practical goal: confirming where the group is.

learnerExperience.evidence: Static model/editor review only; the flow is short and supported, but real learner timing, confusion between I am and we are, and speech-recognition behavior remain untested.

limitations: No independent human or real learner test has been performed.
The lesson establishes only affirmative We are in a bounded location pattern, not the wider pronoun or be paradigm.
The elliptical prompts What time? and Room one? depend on the shared reception/schedule context.
Final ElevenLabs prosody and delayed retention remain unmeasured.
resolvedFindings: Selected CEFR-J we are instead of the slightly higher-listed he/she is because the established community-center scenario gives we an immediate, non-artificial group referent.
No new lexical target was forced merely to satisfy a preference; due At six and known room-number components receive functional reuse instead.
Room one/two remain productive combinations of independent words and the final task changes the room filler to preserve generativity.
Story continuation points to Lesson 20, the latest earlier episode of EN-A1-COMMUNITY, while Lesson 14 remains a pedagogical review source for the original room-choice skill.
Sentence-order reconstruction now uses a dedicated model Turn whose audio text is exactly We are in room two., rather than reusing the longer dialogue response No. We are in room two.
